title: OpPhi loop-carried SSA + real multi-tile coopmat matmul + working tiled attention
strengths: Root cause is precisely identified and well-evidenced: emit_for_range emits structured CFG but never OpPhi for non-Function-storage (SSA) bindings; coopmat bindings have no OpVariable so every loop trip re-reads the pre-header OpConstantNull instead of the per-trip result. The 'every trip reads the same initial id' failure mode is a clean SSA invariant violation, not a heuristic diagnosis.

The phi-first-in-header ordering requirement (SPIR-V §2.4 'All OpPhi instructions must be the first instructions in a block') is correctly specified and its implications for the induction-load / OpLoopMerge placement are explicitly worked through in §A.5. This avoids the classic spirv-val rejection that trips up many SPIR-V emitters.

Mechanism 1 (post-body dr-level insert at header head) is fully viable in rspirv 0.12: `Builder::insert_into_block(InsertPoint::Begin, inst)` and `Builder::select_block(Some(idx))` are both public APIs in rspirv 0.12.0+sdk-1.3.268.0 (confirmed in the installed source at dr/build/mod.rs lines 126-150 and 314-329). The pre-allocation of both phi result id and latch label, body emission, then select_back-to-header + insert_into_block(Begin) pattern is clean and mirrors the existing current_block_label pattern (which already reads module.functions[fi].blocks[bi] by index). Mechanism 2 (OpCopyObject placeholder) is a valid fallback and OpCopyObject on coopmat types is legal per SPIR-V spec §3.32.2 (OpCopyObject is typeless, operating on any type including opaque coopmat).

The scalars-stay-on-Function-storage decision is architecturally sound and risk-reducing: reduction.axc/AT-1606 proves the scalar loop-carried path works today; touching it would be pure regression risk. The coopmat-specific detection (coopmat_binding_ids.contains(B)) is the minimal surgical change. This mirrors the existing body.rs Let handler that already branches on coopmat_binding_ids (line ~481).

OQ-A honesty split is correct and verifiable: matmul_shared_f32.axc explicitly uses `let mut acc: f32 = 0.0f32; acc = acc + a_val * b_val;` — a SCALAR let-mut pattern that goes through Function storage (the existing HirStmt::Let path writes to an OpVariable). Reading the source confirms the acc accumulator is f32, not matrix[...], so it cannot be the OpPhi gap. The gpu=0.0 for f32 is indeed a separate kernel-logic issue. The file also uses `let local_row: u32 = gid(1u32)` and `let tile_row: u32 = gid(1u32)` — both are gid(1), which is the global invocation ID, not a within-workgroup local ID. In a @workgroup(16,16,1) kernel the correct within-tile local_row would be local_invocation_id, not global_id — this is precisely the index-math bug the design diagnoses.

OQ-B (HIR rebind id stability) is correctly identified as the highest-risk real codegen change and Pattern B (let mut + HirStmt::Assign) is the right mandate. The current HirStmt::Assign handler at body.rs:496-503 always calls b.store — which is wrong for a coopmat binding (no OpVariable was allocated in the prelude). Adding `if em.coopmat_binding_ids.contains(binding) { em.var_ids.insert(*binding, val_id); } else { b.store(...) }` is symmetric to the existing Let branch and is minimal.

The GLSL.std.450 + Vulkan memory model co-existence concern for tiled_attention (OQ-C) is resolvable: tiled_attention.axc uses only f32 scalars — NO coopmat — so emit.rs will choose `OpMemoryModel Logical GLSL450` (not Vulkan) for that kernel. The GLSL.std.450 extended-instruction-set is the standard companion to GLSL450 memory model. For a hypothetical future f32-attention-plus-coopmat kernel using Vulkan memory model, GLSL.std.450 OpExtInstImport is still valid (Vulkan SPIR-V spec §A 'Extended Instruction Sets' allows OpExtInstImport under both memory models). This is confirmed by rust-gpu which imports GLSL.std.450 for math builtins in Vulkan compute shaders (see rust-gpu/crates/rustc_codegen_spirv/src/codegen_cx/entry.rs).

The detection rule (§A.3) is conservative and correct: it excludes scalars by construction (not in coopmat_binding_ids), excludes bindings first defined inside the loop (condition b: must have a var_ids entry at loop entry), and scans only the current loop level (condition c: descend_into_nested_loops=false). This prevents double-phi on a binding carried by an inner loop only, and correctly handles the outer-phi-as-inner-pre-header composition described in §A.7.

AT-1700..1704 cover the complete test surface: scalar-no-phi regression (1700), coopmat phi well-formedness with predecessor-label walk (1701), nested loop composition (1702), zero-trip merge-value correctness (1703), and continue-skip conservative rejection (1704). The methodology mirrors the proven AT-117/118 predecessor-walk test pattern from M1.1. spirv-val Vulkan_1_1 is the final gate on all tests.

The competitive TFLOPS methodology (MIN-of-10, GpuTimestamp, labeled datasheet ESTIMATE, NOT asserted >= any ratio) is the right honest reporting approach. The 3.6% naive GEMM result from M3.1.5 is the known comparison point; any coopmat+shared-staged kernel will exceed it, but the design correctly refrains from target-asserting the result.

The bench separation (new resident_matmul_competitive.rs, DO NOT CHANGE resident_matmul.rs IDs) cleanly preserves AT-1711's bench-id regression guard while adding the new measurement. The additive-only API requirement is consistently enforced throughout.
The acceptance test IDs (AT-1700..1704 new + AT-1620/1621/1622/1630 upgrades) are in the correct M3.3 range and do not collide with M3.2's AT-1600..1636.
concerns: Minor — Mechanism 1 requires select_block back to the header after body emission. The Coder needs to capture the header block index BEFORE begin_block(header_label) is called (since selected_block() returns the index of the most recently opened block, and after body+continue+merge blocks are opened, the header is no longer the selected block). The design says 'pre-allocate the phi result id and latch label' but does not explicitly say 'capture header_block_idx = b.selected_block().unwrap() + 1 immediately after begin_block(Some(header_label)) succeeds'. This is a one-line addition the Coder must not forget. The coder_handoff_notes should emphasize capturing the header block index right after opening it, not after building the body. The alternative is to capture the block count before opening the header and compute the index as (block_count_before + 0) — either works. The design is not wrong, just implicit; low risk because the test suite (AT-1701 predecessor walk) will catch any mis-selection.

Minor — The zero-trip post-loop invariant (§A.7: after emit_for_range returns, var_ids[B] = phi_id, NOT latch_value) requires an explicit assignment after the merge block is opened. The design mandates this but the coder_handoff_notes mention it only briefly ('set var_ids[B] = phi_id for every carried B on emit_for_range exit'). A misimplementation would leave var_ids[B] = latch_value after the body, causing a post-loop coopmat_store to reference a value produced inside the loop body — which is not dominated by the merge block and would be spirv-val rejected. AT-1703's 'store source id == phi id' assertion guards this, but the Coder should be aware it requires an EXPLICIT re-set after opening the merge block, not a natural fall-through.

Minor — tiled_attention.axc uses a Taylor exp approximation (`1 + x + x^2/2`) while the design recommends replacing it with exp2-based exp. Both OQ-C options are acceptable (Taylor with matching CPU ref, or real exp2). The current Taylor approximation suffers from accuracy loss when |x| > ~1, but for small score differences (scores shifted by max_score) the approximation is adequate for AT-1630's 1e-3 tolerance. The real risk is consistency: if the GPU uses Taylor and the CPU reference uses `exp()`, the test will FAIL at 1e-3 for any moderate score variance. The design correctly mandates 'CPU reference MUST use the IDENTICAL exp' — the Coder must not forget to mirror whichever branch is chosen in the CPU reference code in dispatch_shared_m32.rs.

Minor — matmul_shared_f32.axc's indexing bug is correctly diagnosed (gid(1) used for BOTH tile_row and local_row at lines 41-44). However the fix is more subtle than it appears: in a Vulkan compute shader, getting the true within-workgroup local invocation ID requires a separate builtin, not gid(). The current AXIOM-Compute HIR/codegen supports `gid(N)` for GlobalInvocationId (confirmed in crates/axc-codegen/src/body.rs gid builtin). The Coder needs to add `local_invocation_id(N)` builtin support OR restructure the kernel to derive tile-local coordinates from `gid mod workgroup_size`. If local_invocation_id is not yet a first-class builtin, this is an implementation scope question. The design scopes it as 'debug the workgroup-dispatch / global-index math' without specifying whether a new builtin is required — the Coder should check during the empirical OQ-A verification step.

Low — The `break` analysis in §A.7 states: 'a break edge goes to MERGE not header, so it does NOT add a header-phi predecessor'. This is correct. However the design also says 'the merge reads phi_id = the value from the predecessor that branched'. The merge block has no OpPhi of its own — it simply reads whatever var_ids[B] resolves to after the loop exits. For a break path, the post-loop read sees the phi_id (because var_ids[B] is left = phi_id on exit). The phi's latch predecessor value came from the trip before the break, which is the correct loop-carried semantics. This is sound; the concern is purely documentation clarity (no change needed).

Low — The OQ-F concern about nested-loop phi composition under spirv-val is well-handled by AT-1702 but there is one edge case not explicitly addressed: if both an inner and outer coopmat phi exist in the same function, spirv-val will check that EVERY phi in EVERY block has its predecessor labels match the CFG predecessors of THAT block. The inner phi's predecessors are {inner_pre-header, inner_latch}; the outer phi's predecessors are {outer_pre-header, outer_latch}. These must not be confused. The design's dominance-tree composition logic is correct; AT-1702 will catch any confusion. No action needed; calling it out for the pessimistic reviewer.
validation_against_existing: SPIR-V 1.3 spec §2.4 (https://registry.khronos.org/SPIR-V/specs/unified1/SPIRV.html#_control_flow): 'All OpPhi instructions must be the first instructions in a block, after the block label.' The design's Mechanism 1 post-inserts at InsertPoint::Begin specifically to satisfy this rule — correct.

SPIR-V 1.3 spec §3.32.13 OpPhi: 'Variable must be one of the (value, parent) pair values where the type of value matches the type of Variable. All of the predecessor blocks of the current block must be listed as parent.' The two-predecessor constraint {pre_header, latch} matches exactly the structured-loop CFG: pre_header branches to header (the initial branch), latch branches back to header (the back-edge). No other block has a direct branch to the header. spirv-val enforces this exactly.

SPIR-V 1.3 spec §2.11 / §3.32.17 OpLoopMerge: 'This instruction must immediately precede either an OpBranch or an OpBranchConditional instruction.' The design's header block ordering (OpPhi first, then induction load, then OpLoopMerge, then OpBranchConditional) satisfies this: OpLoopMerge still immediately precedes OpBranchConditional (phis are before both). Confirmed also by existing emit_for_range doc-comment at body.rs:720-737.

rspirv 0.12.0+sdk-1.3.268.0 (installed at ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/rspirv-0.12.0+sdk-1.3.268.0/dr/build/mod.rs): `Builder::insert_into_block(InsertPoint::Begin, inst)` is a public stable API that inserts at index 0 of the currently selected block's instruction vec. `Builder::select_block(Some(idx))` is also public and stable. Both are available — Mechanism 1 is fully implementable without module-surgery. `Builder::module_mut()` at line 215 also provides direct `&mut dr::Module` access as a fallback.

rspirv 0.12 dr::Instruction::new: constructing a bare OpPhi instruction via `rspirv::dr::Instruction::new(Op::Phi, Some(result_type), Some(result_id), operands)` with `operands = vec![Operand::IdRef(v0), Operand::IdRef(p0), Operand::IdRef(v1), Operand::IdRef(p1)]` is the standard dr-level construction pattern, used in practice by rust-gpu (see gfx-rs/rust-gpu/crates/rustc_codegen_spirv/src/builder/phi.rs which constructs OpPhi via dr::Instruction for phis in loops).

GLSL.std.450 + Vulkan memory model co-existence: The Vulkan SPIR-V environment spec (https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html Appendix A) explicitly permits importing GLSL.std.450 extended instruction set in Vulkan compute shaders regardless of OpMemoryModel choice. For tiled_attention.axc (pure f32, no coopmat), emit.rs chooses GLSL450 memory model (body.rs emit.rs line 160: coopmat=false path), so the standard GLSL.std.450 import is used without any conflict.

SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix spec (https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Registry/blob/main/extensions/KHR/SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix.asciidoc): OpCooperativeMatrixMulAddKHR result type must match the accumulator type (type of operand 3). The existing emit_coopmat_mul_add correctly passes result_ty as the accumulator CoopMatKey. The loop-carried phi emits OpPhi with the SAME accumulator type (fetched from coopmat_type_cache.get_or_emit for the accumulator key) — type-consistent.

The project's own AT-117 and AT-118 test methodology (body.rs lines 1851-1881) demonstrates that OpPhi predecessor-label walking via rspirv dr::Module.functions[fi].blocks[bi].instructions is already used and tested in this codebase. The new AT-1701 test is a direct extension of this proven pattern to loop-carried coopmat phis.

IREE/MLIR SPIR-V lowering (https://github.com/iree-org/iree/blob/main/compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/SPIRV/Utils/SPIRVUtils.cpp): IREE's loop->SPIR-V lowering also uses the two-pass approach: allocate phi result ids, emit body, then back-fill phi operands. This validates the two-pass strategy at production scale.

OQ-A.position: CORRECT — the honesty split is accurate and the diagnosis is verifiable from source.
OQ-A.justification: matmul_shared_f32.axc uses `let mut acc: f32 = 0.0f32;` — an f32 scalar which gets an OpVariable in Function storage via the prelude (body.rs lines 437-444: scalar path). HirStmt::Let for a scalar stores to that OpVariable; loop-carried reads do OpLoad from it — this works today (reduction.axc is bit-exact). The real bug in matmul_shared_f32 is at lines 41-44: `let local_row: u32 = gid(1u32); let tile_col: u32 = gid(0u32);` — gid() returns GlobalInvocationId, so local_row == tile_row for every invocation. There is NO differentiation between the invocation's tile-level position and its within-tile position. For a @workgroup(16,16,1) kernel covering a 16x16 output tile, each invocation computes gid(1) as its GLOBAL row, not its row within the tile. The indexing into a_tile and b_tile will be globally-indexed rather than tile-locally-indexed, producing incorrect staging and wrong outputs — entirely independent of OpPhi. The Coder should confirm empirically (compile and dispatch matmul_shared_f32 with a corrected dispatch geometry on a 16x16 output fixture — one workgroup, gid(0) in [0,15], gid(1) in [0,15]) to isolate the scalar-path bug.
OQ-A.risk: LOW — the design is honest about this distinction and scopes PART B's f32 debug separately. No risk of the Coder confusing the two bugs if they follow the empirical verification step first.

OQ-B.position: Pattern B (let mut + HirStmt::Assign) MANDATORY. The HIR rebind risk is REAL but tractable.
OQ-B.justification: If lower.rs allocates a fresh BindingId for each `let acc = ...` occurrence (even if same name), detection (§A.3.c) would fail because the outer id != inner id. The safest path is Pattern B: `let mut acc: matrix[f16,16,16,accumulator] = coopmat_zero(); acc = coopmat_mul_add(a_mat,b_mat,acc);` using HirStmt::Assign with the stable outer binding id. The required body.rs change (HirStmt::Assign coopmat branch: SSA rebind instead of b.store) is surgical and mirrors the existing Let handler. The Coder must confirm lower.rs behaviour before writing the kernel — if re-let reuses the same BindingId for same-name same-scope bindings, Pattern A also works; if not, Pattern B is mandatory. The typecheck.rs change (allow `let mut` on accumulator matrix + reassignment type-check) is straightforward.
OQ-B.risk: MEDIUM if Coder skips the lower.rs verification; LOW if they check first as instructed.

OQ-C.position: RECOMMEND real exp2-based exp via mathfn.rs, but Taylor with matching CPU reference is also acceptable.
OQ-C.justification: For AT-1630's 1e-3 tolerance, Taylor `1+x+x^2/2` is accurate for |x| < ~1 (after score - max_score the differences are typically small for well-conditioned attention inputs). The real risk is CPU-GPU mismatch: if the GPU uses Taylor and the CPU uses stdlib `exp()`, the test WILL fail at 1e-3 for any fixture with moderate score variance. The real exp2 path (OpExtInst GLSL.std.450 Exp2 for a pure-f32 kernel — no coopmat conflict) is more honest and bit-stable; the CPU reference uses `(x * LOG2_E).exp2()` which is trivially matchable. Either is fine AS LONG AS the CPU ref uses the identical computation. The mathfn.rs module (additive, small) is the cleaner design even if only used by one kernel.
OQ-C.risk: LOW either way, conditional on CPU-reference consistency.

OQ-D.position: Mechanism 1 is VIABLE and PREFERRED in rspirv 0.12.
OQ-D.justification: Confirmed: `Builder::insert_into_block(InsertPoint::Begin, dr::Instruction)` and `Builder::select_block(Some(idx))` are both public stable APIs in rspirv 0.12.0 (dr/build/mod.rs lines 126-150, 314-329). The Coder must capture `header_block_idx = b.selected_block().unwrap()` immediately after `begin_block(Some(header_label))` succeeds. After body+continue+merge emission, call `b.select_block(Some(header_block_idx))`, then for each carried binding in reverse declaration order: `b.insert_into_block(InsertPoint::Begin, phi_inst)`. Then re-select the merge block. This is clean, requires no module surgery beyond the documented select_block API, and will be spirv-val verified. Mechanism 2 (OpCopyObject) is a valid fallback if Mechanism 1 proves awkward in practice.

OQ-E.position: A single-tile-per-workgroup shared-staged coopmat kernel will exceed the 3.6% naive baseline but is unlikely to approach cuBLAS territory for a >=256x256x256 problem. Honest reporting is the RIGHT call and is the thesis-relevant metric.
OQ-E.justification: A single 16x16 coopmat tile per workgroup at 32 threads covers 256 FLOPs per MulAdd (16x16x16x2). For a 256x256x256 problem that is 256x256x256x2 = 33.5 MFLOPs total. With RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell's tensor core throughput, the theoretical peak for f16 coopmat is high, but a single-tile-per-workgroup design leaves most SMs idle — only 256/16 × 256/16 = 16x16 = 256 workgroups, each with 32 threads. The Blackwell SM count (132 on RTX PRO 6000) means at most 132 active workgroups simultaneously; 256 workgroups gives some pipelining but tile reuse and SM occupancy will be far below cuBLAS. Realistic expectation: 5-15% of the cuBLAS f32 datasheet estimate (125 TFLOPS). This is above the 3.6% naive GEMM and demonstrates coopmat+shared staging working on real hardware — a meaningful thesis milestone. The design commits to reporting WHATEVER it measures, which is the correct approach. A same-machine cuBLAS A/B is out of thesis scope (CUDA-free); the datasheet-labeled estimate comparison is sufficient for the thesis claim 'one annotated source → portable coopmat SPIR-V'.
OQ-E.risk: ZERO risk from reporting honestly. If the number is low, ROADMAP should note 'multi-tile coopmat tiling (wider workgroup dispatch covering the full problem) deferred to M3.x' rather than spinning the result.

OQ-F.position: Composition holds under spirv-val provided each phi's predecessor labels match ITS loop's CFG predecessors.
OQ-F.justification: The inner loop header's predecessors are its own {inner_pre_header, inner_latch} — these are determined by the CFG, not by any outer loop structure. spirv-val validates each phi independently against the CFG. The outer-phi-as-inner-pre-header-operand pattern is valid because the outer phi id dominates the inner loop entry (the inner loop is nested inside the outer loop body). AT-1702 will catch any label confusion. No design change needed.

test_suggestions: Strong suggestion: AT-1701 should explicitly assert that the phi result id matches what var_ids[B] resolves to in the post-loop context (i.e., that emit_for_range leaves var_ids[B] = phi_id on exit). This is currently covered by AT-1703 (store source == phi id) but having an explicit 'loop exit var_ids check' in AT-1701 as well would guard the zero-trip edge case even for non-zero-trip paths.

Consider adding a spirv-dis text check for AT-1701 that asserts the phi appears as the first non-label instruction (by checking that the instruction index in the block is 0) in addition to the predecessor-label walk. The rspirv dr walk can count instructions before the phi; if any non-phi non-label instruction precedes it, the test should fail even if spirv-val passes (spirv-val may or may not catch instruction ordering violations in all edge cases).

AT-1621 (matmul_shared_f32 bit-exact) should document in the test code whether local_invocation_id builtin support was added or whether the kernel was restructured to use gid mod workgroup_size. This is important for understanding the scope of change and prevents future confusion.

The 50 GB cap assertion for the competitive matmul bench (AT-1710 / resident_matmul_competitive.rs) should be an explicit `assert!(total_bytes < 50 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)` before any allocation — the design mentions it in edge_cases but it must appear as actual code in the bench.
summary: The M3.3 design is sound and should be approved. The root cause analysis is precise: emit_for_range produces correct structured CFG but coopmat (SSA) bindings have no OpVariable, so a loop-carried coopmat accumulator re-reads its initial OpConstantNull every iteration. The fix — OpPhi at the loop header with operands {pre_header_value, latch_value} — is a standard SSA technique. The SPIR-V ordering constraint (phis first in the block, before induction load and OpLoopMerge) is correctly specified. The rspirv 0.12 implementation path via insert_into_block(InsertPoint::Begin) + select_block(Some(header_idx)) is confirmed viable from the installed library source. The OQ-A honesty split is independently verifiable from the matmul_shared_f32.axc source (gid(1) used as both tile_row and local_row — provably a dispatch/index bug, not the OpPhi gap). Pattern B (let mut + HirStmt::Assign) is the correct HIR pattern and the required body.rs Assign handler extension is minimal and symmetric to the existing Let handler. Acceptance tests AT-1700..1704 provide strong structural coverage with spirv-val as the final gate. Competitive TFLOPS reporting is appropriately honest (reported as measured, labeled as datasheet estimate, not asserted). No design revision is needed before implementation begins.
coder_guidance_additions: Capture `header_block_idx = b.selected_block().unwrap()` IMMEDIATELY after `begin_block(Some(header_label))` succeeds — before opening any subsequent block. This index is needed for the post-body `select_block(Some(header_block_idx))` call when inserting phis.

After opening the merge block at emit_for_range exit, EXPLICITLY set `em.var_ids.insert(B, phi_id)` for every carried binding B — do not let the latch value remain in var_ids. AT-1703 guards this but it must be an intentional assignment.

For the matmul_shared_f32 local-row bug: check whether `local_invocation_id(N)` builtin is supported before restructuring the kernel. If not available, derive tile-local coordinates from `gid(N) - tile_coord * TILE_SIZE` — this works with the existing gid() builtin and requires no new HIR support.
